stories.headline: India 'cockroach' leaders who called on election chief to quit are freed from jail
stories.title: India 'cockroach' leaders who called on election chief to quit are freed from jail
stories.summary: Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were accused of breaking into an unauthorised protest venue in Delhi.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Two leaders of the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) have been freed from jail a week after they were arrested for trespassing at a banned protest site in Delhi.
Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka walked out of Tihar jail hours after a magistrate ordered their release.
They had been detained by police and jailed after they crossed barricades and climbed over the locked gate at Jantar Mantar.
The men, who denied wrongdoing, have been calling on India's chief election commissioner to resign.
Critics accuse the commission of manipulating voter rolls to benefit India's governing party, charges the commission rejects.
A special executive magistrate court in Delhi, passed their release order, legal news website Bar and Bench reported.
After bail was granted, Das told reporters from a police van: "Truth alone triumphs.
Das and Ranka are key leaders of the CJP, which began as an internet joke in May after India's top judge compared unemployed young people to "cockroaches".
The CJP is not a registered political party, but a collective which began by mobilising thousands of young people to protest over leaked exam papers.
By July it had emerged as a major force.
A march towards parliament that month ended in clashes with police, drawing wider attention to the movement and increasing pressure on the government.

stories.headline: Marco Rubio in India: Trade deal in sight, oil on the agenda
stories.title: Marco Rubio in India: Trade deal in sight, oil on the agenda
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said India and the United States were “very, very close” to finalising a trade deal, with only a few issues left to resolve, during his two-day visit to India on October 20-21. His meetings also focused on expanding energy trade, including the possibility of Indian refineries processing more Venezuelan crude.“I would say we're about as close as you can be without having executed the agreement,” Rubio told reporters in Mumbai on Tuesday. “I think there's a small number of items to wrap up, so I think that will happen shortly.” He said the US was optimistic about reaching an agreement soon, but did not give a date for its conclusion.US President Donald Trump also said on Tuesday that the two countries were “pretty close” to an agreement. “They want to make a deal. We're going to make a deal. Pretty close, yeah,” he told reporters at the White House, adding that it would be “a much different kind of deal” from previous agreements, without elaborating.Rubio also met External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in Mumbai before travelling to Jamnagar in Gujarat the following day to visit Reliance Industries' refining complex. After the meeting, Jaishankar said the two sides discussed trade, energy, technology, defence, people-to-people ties, and regional developments.Also Read: Big items done, confident we will have India-US trade deal: Sergio Gor“Pleased to meet US Secretary Rubio in Mumbai today. We shared views on further advancing our ties, focusing on trade, energy, technology, defence, and people-to-people ties. Also exchanged views on regional developments,” Jaishankar said in a post on X. India's Ministry of External Affairs said both sides had welcomed progress in negotiations on the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement and reaffirmed their commitment to working towards its early conclusion.Trade TalksTrade negotiations between India and the US have been ongoing since Donald Trump returned to the White House in January 2025, with differences over tariffs and market access delaying an agreement. India's continued purchases of Russian crude have added to tensions between the two countries.Washington is seeking greater access to India's market and ways to address its trade deficit, while New Delhi has pushed for preferential access for Indian exporters and greater certainty over US tariffs.Earlier this month, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said the negotiations had reached a “plateau”, with further concessions likely to be “very, very difficult” for both sides. She said the talks were continuing and noted that addressing the US trade deficit with India was a major consideration for Washington.On October 15, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement had been finalised and was undergoing legal drafting. He said India wanted to secure a competitive advantage over peer countries before the agreement was operationalised.US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor had also said last week that the broad framework and major elements of the agreement were settled, though work on the remaining issues continued.Also Read: India’s economic resilience shines through despite global headwinds: CEARubio said that both sides needed to agree on the meaning of the language before announcing a deal. In an interview with Network18, on Tuesday, he explained, “The difference is when you are friends, when you are allies, when you have so much in common, that's what allows you to bridge those differences and come up with something that's mutually beneficial.” Rubio added that the negotiations had reached the stage of working through technical details. He said, “I'm not personally negotiating it because it's done through our Trade Representative. But I know, and have been very involved in watching it happen, that it is something we anticipate seeing in a matter of weeks, not months.”Reliance, Venezuelan crude and energy talksSpeaking to reporters in Mumbai, Rubio said India had repeatedly expressed a desire to diversify its energy sources. “It's not easy to do that from one day to the next,” he said, adding that India had made “some substantial progress” and that the US could supply some of its energy needs.“We have discussed Venezuela and other countries, and I think it's in our interest to have strong allies with diverse energy portfolios,” he said. Rubio also said he would discuss Venezuelan crude with Reliance. The company has processed the country's heavy crude in the past and has refining capacity suited to those grades.“They've done so in the past. They have the capability to refine heavy crude,” Rubio said. “As more and more Venezuelan oil comes online, it's something they can do.”He also referred to oil concessions held by Indian companies in Venezuela and said they could increase production there. Rubio said sanctions could present obstacles that would need to be addressed.During his visit to Jamnagar on Wednesday, Rubio said the visit was an opportunity to see Reliance's operations and discuss its presence in global energy markets. Reliance operates two refineries at Jamnagar, with a combined crude-processing capacity of about 1.4 million barrels per day.Rubio's visit comes as the US-Iran war has continued to push energy costs higher. Renewed attacks on shipping and energy infrastructure in West Asia have led Brent crude futures to rise above the $100 mark. On Wednesday morning, Brent rose to $110.11 a barrel, nearing a five-month high. The International Energy Agency has said global diesel and gas oil exports fell by nearly 700,000 barrels per day year on year in September, with losses from Russia and West Asia only partly offset by higher supplies elsewhere. The agency expects the diesel market to remain tight well into 2027, as supply disruptions, high shipping costs and refinery constraints limit the recovery in availability.Also Read: Explained: How Trump’s new tariff law impacts IndiaRussian oil and tariffsIndia's purchases of Russian crude have strained relations with the United States. In September, the US passed legislation allowing tariffs of up to 100 percent on goods from major buyers of Russian oil, including India. Trump waived the relevant provisions on October 16 and announced a 60-day review period.Rubio has said the impact of tariffs on US relations with India must be weighed alongside Washington's objectives in dealing with Russia. He has argued that energy supply, prices and countries' ability to find alternative sources need to be considered when Washington makes sanctions decisions.New Delhi has argued that energy imports should reflect supply availability, prices, and the need to maintain market stability. The US, meanwhile, has suggested India diversify its sources, including through increased purchases of American energy.India imports more than 85 percent of its crude oil requirements and has continued to buy Russian oil despite pressure from Washington.During his visit, Rubio also met Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani and Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran in Mumbai, paid tribute to the victims of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks at the Taj Mahal Palace hotel, and attended a reception marking the 250th anniversary of US independence. Rubio is scheduled to leave Jamnagar early on Thursday, October 22, concluding his visit to India.

stories.headline: Beyond telecom: Why investors may pay a premium for Jio's IPO
stories.title: Beyond telecom: Why investors may pay a premium for Jio's IPO
stories.summary: As Jio Platform’s initial public offering (IPO) opens for subscription on Wednesday, investors may not view it through the same lens as a traditional telecom offering. While Jio's market-leading mobile business provides scale and cash flows, the company's next phase of growth is expected to come from businesses beyond telecom.With much of its infrastructure already in place, Jio Platform is shifting its focus from network rollout to monetisation. The real investment bet goes well beyond subscriber additions, tariff increases, or market share gains. Instead, investors are betting on Jio's ability to unlock value from one of India's largest digital ecosystems, spanning artificial intelligence, cloud computing, enterprise technology, broadband and connected services.“Its future growth is expected to be supported by tariff rationalisation, migration from 2G to 4G and 5G, higher data consumption, home broadband expansion and increasing enterprise adoption of cloud and digital solutions,” analysts at SBI Securities say. They add that additional monetisation opportunities may emerge from AI-led services, digital applications, satellite connectivity, and overseas deployment of its proprietary technology platforms.The broader digital opportunity, rather than telecom earnings alone, is therefore what could justify a premium valuation for Jio Platform.Sudeep Anand, research analyst, Systematix also feels Jio Platforms is well placed to benefit from India’s accelerating digitalisation, supported by its large and diversified customer base, pan-India network and strong position in wireless data consumption.“Its integrated digital ecosystem spanning connectivity, broadband, digital platforms, cloud and enterprise services provides multiple avenues for sustained growth. Strong subscriber engagement, rising data usage, tariff-led average revenue per user (ARPU) expansion and increasing penetration of JioFiber and JioAirFiber should support revenue growth, while continued investments in ‘5G, AI and cloud infrastructure’ are expected to strengthen its technology leadership,” Anand explains.Anand elaborates that Jio Platforms offers an attractive opportunity to participate in India’s long-term digital and connectivity growth story.Also Read: Jio taps stock markets for Rs30,200 crore in landmark IPO“While elevated capex requirements, competitive intensity, regulatory interventions and execution risks remain key monitorable, the company’s market leadership, robust profitability, strong cash-generation profile and multiple structural growth levers provide comfort on its long-term prospects,” he adds.Why are markets paying attention?Ahead of its IPO for the public subscription, the company has already raised Rs 8,109.84 crore from 212 anchor investors. Some marquee global investors in the anchor book include like BlackRock, Capital Group, Fidelity Investments, T. Rowe Price, Schroders, JPMorgan Asset Management, Franklin Templeton, Invesco, and Prudential.The three-day sale will close for subscription on October 23. The offering comprises a fresh issue of 27 crore shares. The Mukesh Ambani-led company aims to raise around Rs 30,200 crore with a price band set at Rs 1,065-1,119 per piece, positioning it among the biggest IPOs ever in India.Jio Platforms' Rs 30,200-crore offering is an entirely fresh issue, which means existing shareholders will not sell any shares through the IPO; instead, the entire proceeds will be used by the company. A large part of the funds—up to Rs 27,500 crore—will be used to pare debt at Reliance Jio Infocomm, while the balance will support general corporate requirements and future growth initiatives.Jio Platforms is India’s largest digital-connectivity platform, with operations spanning mobile and fixed broadband, enterprise connectivity and digital services.Through Reliance Jio Infocomm, Jio Platforms was the first operator in India to launch a standalone 5G network and has supported rapid adoption of 5G services across the country. As of 1QFY27, the company had 284.9 million 5G customers, representing the third-largest 5G customer base globally. Its 5G network supports applications such as ultra-high-definition and 4K video streaming, cloud gaming, augmented reality and virtual reality.Over the years, Jio Platforms has attracted a range of bluechip global investors, including Meta, Google, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, KKR-backed Omicron Asia Holdings, General Atlantic Singapore, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority-backed Platinum Jasmine, and TPG-managed India Markets. However, Reliance Industries continues to hold a controlling 66.43 percent stake in the company, retaining a firm grip over the group's most valuable digital asset.Valuation gameAccording to analysts at Geojit Investments, at the upper price band of the IPO, Jio is valued at 15 times FY26 enterprise value (EV)/EBITDA on a post-issue basis, implying a premium to industry peers. “This premium is justified by Jio’s market leadership, improving monetisation, strong cash flow generation, and substantial long-term optionality beyond its core telecom business,” they say.The analysts explain that the IPO-led deleveraging is expected to further strengthen the balance sheet. While the near- term upside may be moderated by the premium valuation, the monetisation of cloud, AI, enterprise solutions, entertainment, digital platforms, and fixed broadband services could emerge as key drivers of earnings growth over the medium to long term.The company benefits from a dominant position in India's mobile broadband market with 533.3 million customers, approximately 49.8 percent wireless broadband market share. Its proprietary technology stack, extensive distribution network and strong brand franchise provide significant competitive advantages and create high barriers to entry, says Rinkle Vira, analyst at Anand Rathi.“Considering its leadership position in India's digital ecosystem, strong profitability, scalable technology platform, robust growth prospects and significant opportunities in AI, enterprise digital services and fixed broadband, the valuation appears reasonable relative to its long-term growth potential,” Vira explains.Also Read: Telecom tariffs back in focus as Airtel and Jio take divergent pathsIndia has a four-player mobile market, and the top three players have a mobile broadband market share of over 97 percent as of June 30, 2026. Jio is themarket leader, followed by Bharti Airtel at 35.47 percent, Vodafone Idea at 12.51 percent and BSNL at 2.20 percent.As of June, Jio also holds the industry’s largest spectrum bank, totalling 26,800.8 MHz, with a 16-year average remaining life. Jio is the only operator in India to have spectrum in low-band, mid-band and millimetre wave (700 MHz, 3300 MHz and 26 GHz) for 5G across all circles.Jio is the first operator in India to launch a standalone 5G network, which operates independently of 4G infrastructure and has advanced capabilities like network slicing and superior low-latency performance. Jio has the third-largest 5G customer base in the world, with 284.9 million customers on 5G as of June. Its standalone architecture across bands supports this scale, delivering average speeds of 198.9 Mbps in Q3 FY2026.“At 33 times FY2026 earnings, valuation is at the lower end versus peers,” say analysts at Canara Securities. They see Jio benefiting from volume-led growth across its mobility, home, and MSME businesses, while bundled media, productivity, and AI solutions provide a clear pathway to ARPU improvement.According to analysts at Shriram Research, at the upper price band, the issue is valued reasonably, which is well-supported by Jio's undisputed market leadership and consistent double- digit EBITDA growth. “The company stands out as a core structural compounder for India's digital economy, underpinned by robust cash generation, declining leverage as IPO proceeds are utilised to repay debt, and rapid adoption of home broadband services,” they say.According to analysts at Shriram Research, Jio Platform's revenue and profitability are poised for sustained expansion, driven by ongoing ARPU hikes, 2G-to-4G/5G subscriber migration, deepening enterprise relationships, and the potential export of its proprietary in-house tech stack to overseas operators.“While regulatory and competitive risks remain, the structural health of the industry and the strength of an integrated digital ecosystem make this an attractive, high-conviction opportunity for medium- to long-term investors,” analysts at Shriram Research add.Part of the Reliance ecosystemFollowing Jio’s listing, Reliance Industries will be India’s largest listed conglomerate, marking a formal generational transition to children Akash, Anant, and Isha Ambani under chairman Mukesh Ambani’s guidance. Reliance Industries met Mukesh Ambani’s 2019 target of becoming net debt-free by 2021 despite the Covid-19 pandemic. The shares of RIL have delivered a 29 percent annualised shareholder return since its 1977 IPO.Meanwhile, celebrating a decade since its launch on September 6, 2026, Jio has grown into India's largest digital connectivity platform, with a customer base of 53 crore with a 60 percent share of India's data traffic.Jio completed India’s nationwide 4G-to-5G standalone migration in 19 months, creating the world’s largest 5G subscriber base outside China at 284.9 million, while users consume 43.7 GB monthly, which is 1.5 times that of the nearest competitor. Since Jio’s 2016 launch, the telecom market has consolidated from 14 to four operators, data prices have fallen from Rs 228 per GB to Rs 7.50 per GB, and speeds have surged from 2.5 Mbps to 68 Mbps.Over FY2024-FY2026, its revenue grew at a 15.8 percent CAGR to Rs 1.47 lakh crore, EBITDA rose 17 percent while net profit jumped 18.43 percent to Rs 30,064 crore.“At the upper price band, the issue is valued at a post-issue FY26 price-to-earnings (PE) multiple of 34.4 times and an enterprise value/subscriber multiple of Rs 20,117, reflecting its scale, earnings growth, technology capabilities and long-term monetisation potential,” say analysts at SBI Securities.As of June, the company and its subsidiaries have applied for 7,220 patents across 4G, 5G, and 6G cloud-native core network architectures, AI-driven network automation, and other digital technologies. This portfolio includes 2,655 patent applications in India and 4,565 filed in international jurisdictions.

“The company stands out as a core structural compounder for India's digital economy, underpinned by robust cash generation, declining leverage as IPO proceeds are utilised to repay debt, and rapid adoption of home broadband services,” they say.

According to analysts at Shriram Research, Jio Platform's revenue and profitability are poised for sustained expansion, driven by ongoing ARPU hikes, 2G-to-4G/5G subscriber migration, deepening enterprise relationships, and the potential export of its proprietary in-house tech stack to overseas operators.

“While regulatory and competitive risks remain, the structural health of the industry and the strength of an integrated digital ecosystem make this an attractive, high-conviction opportunity for medium- to long-term investors,” analysts at Shriram Research add.

Part of the Reliance ecosystemFollowing Jio’s listing, Reliance Industries will be India’s largest listed conglomerate, marking a formal generational transition to children Akash, Anant, and Isha Ambani under chairman Mukesh Ambani’s guidance.
Reliance Industries met Mukesh Ambani’s 2019 target of becoming net debt-free by 2021 despite the Covid-19 pandemic.
The shares of RIL have delivered a 29 percent annualised shareholder return since its 1977 IPO.

Jio completed India’s nationwide 4G-to-5G standalone migration in 19 months, creating the world’s largest 5G subscriber base outside China at 284.9 million, while users consume 43.7 GB monthly, which is 1.5 times that of the nearest competitor.
Since Jio’s 2016 launch, the telecom market has consolidated from 14 to four operators, data prices have fallen from Rs 228 per GB to Rs 7.50 per GB, and speeds have surged from 2.5 Mbps to 68 Mbps.
Over FY2024-FY2026, its revenue grew at a 15.8 percent CAGR to Rs 1.47 lakh crore, EBITDA rose 17 percent while net profit jumped 18.43 percent to Rs 30,064 crore.

“At the upper price band, the issue is valued at a post-issue FY26 price-to-earnings (PE) multiple of 34.4 times and an enterprise value/subscriber multiple of Rs 20,117, reflecting its scale, earnings growth, technology capabilities and long-term monetisation potential,” say analysts at SBI Securities.

As of June, the company and its subsidiaries have applied for 7,220 patents across 4G, 5G, and 6G cloud-native core network architectures, AI-driven network automation, and other digital technologies.
This portfolio includes 2,655 patent applications in India and 4,565 filed in international jurisdictions.

Valuation gameAccording to analysts at Geojit Investments, at the upper price band of the IPO, Jio is valued at 15 times FY26 enterprise value (EV)/EBITDA on a post-issue basis, implying a premium to industry peers.
India has a four-player mobile market, and the top three players have a mobile broadband market share of over 97 percent as of June 30, 2026.
As of June, Jio also holds the industry’s largest spectrum bank, totalling 26,800.8 MHz, with a 16-year average remaining life.

stories.headline: Ladakh High Court bench begins regular hearings
stories.title: Ladakh High Court bench begins regular hearings
stories.summary: Leh, Oct 21: A historic chapter in Indian judicial history unfolded on Wednesday when Chief Justice of the High Court of J&K and Ladakh, Dr Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Sanjay Parihar presided over the first regular division bench at Leh. The newly established Ladakh Bench of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh located at a breath-taking height of over 11,500 feet above sea level, began regular hearing of the cases from today. The day began with the hearing by the Division Bench in which the Chief Justice heard the matters through virtual mode while Justice Sanjay Parihar was present physically at the Ladakh Bench. After the conclusion of the hearing of five listed Division Bench matters, Justice Sanjay Parihar sat singly and dealt with as many as 60 matters listed before the single bench. Today’s proceedings made use of technology to facilitate a sort of hybrid hearing with the Chief Justice hearing through Virtual Mode and Justice Sanjay Parihar doing physical hearing. Justice Parihar said that the identification of the 65 cases that were listed today reflects the initial effort to organise and facilitate the hearing of matters concerning litigants from Ladakh. He added that the successful commencement of regular judicial hearings today by the Chief Justice in such a high-altitude location is a landmark achievement in the country’s judicial infrastructure and commitment to ensuring that geographical barriers do not become obstacles to justice. The establishment of the Ladakh Bench is a significant step in strengthening the reach of constitutional institutions to remote and geographically challenging regions of the country. Earlier, litigants from Leh, Kargil and other far-flung areas of Ladakh would undertake lengthy journeys to Srinagar or Jammu for proceedings before the High Court. The commencement of hearings here is also encouraging for the legal fraternity of Ladakh including advocates. It may be mentioned that the Ladakh Bench of J& K High court was formally inaugurated by the Chief Justice of India, Justice Surya Kanton October 18, 2026, at Melongthang, Leh.
